title: Dungeon Seeker
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Bullied high-schooler Junpei Takeda is summoned to another world by a whimsical 'god' along with his bully Shouta Kido and his childhood friend Noriko Tatsumiya. His stats are weaker than a farmer's, but he can learn skills from enemies he defeats; after months of survival, Noriko and Kido trick him into the Sacrificial Labyrinth, which no one has escaped, and he fights through it driven by revenge (Alpha Manga blurb via AniList; MangaUpdates; MyAnimeList synopsis).
life_message: The weak can become strong through endurance, and betrayal is answered with revenge.

content.note: AniList Gore (72); MU Blood and Gore, Cannibalism, Torture; a MAL reviewer says the lead is 'ok with killing people'.
Deadly labyrinth and despair; MAL reviewer compares its 'depression' to Made in Abyss; AniList Horror genre.
AniList Ecchi genre; MU lists Rape, Gang Rape, Partial Nudity at low vote counts (to verify; possibly higher).
Bullying and betrayal breed hatred (AniList and MU Bullying, Hatred; MAL synopsis: 'constantly bullied').
Revenge is the hero's drive (AniList Revenge 92; MAL).

dominant: Revenge on betrayers; survival of the strongest; whimsical, indifferent god

frames.aligns: Bullying and betrayal shown as wrongs.
frames.concerns: Revenge as the goal; gore; tagged sexual violence (to verify).
Hatred nurtured; gore and possible sexual violence.
Hatred, gore and a whimsical god figure.
Private vengeance; lascivious and cruel content.
Tagged sexual violence and glorified revenge.

frames.aligns: Sincerity betrayed is shown as grave.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Betrayal answered by personal revenge (AniList Revenge; MAL synopsis).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Lawless labyrinth; only strength counts (MU Survival).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Even a childhood friend betrays; trust shrinks to self (MU Betrayal).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Status rankings are overturned by the 'weakest' (blurb).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: A whimsical 'god' and game-like stats, no faith (blurb; MU Game Elements).

folkways.japan: Reflects the Japanese isekai revenge subgenre, where school bullying (ijime) is carried into a fantasy world.

delivery.evidence: No review comments on lecturing; message carried by revenge plot (to verify).

personified.ideology: The bullied made strong; revenge as justice
Bullying and domination of the weak

delivery.note: The bully and the betrayer are the story's targets; whether they are given motives beyond cruelty was not checked.

winners_losers: Junpei grows strong and pursues revenge; his betrayers are set up to lose. Sympathy goes to the bullied avenger.
